figmaBuildPlan.tokenProfileHint: Dark theme with authority-led visual language; use a strong brand-primary hero, logo-first trust band, and media-led product storytelling. Prefer Plus Jakarta Sans headings with Inter body for a clean enterprise/AI feel.

sections.notes: Use full-width dark hero with strong headline overlap only within hero container, not outside it. Include headline, subheadline, supporting line, primary CTA, and empty secondary CTA slot only if design system requires symmetry. Keep copy centered; no extra lead magnet. Use large typography sized for 8-11 words. Add a subtle AI/generative visual treatment but keep text legible on dark background.

Make this the dominant trust signal. Use a horizontal logo strip with multiple partner/customer logos as the primary visual element, plus a compact customer trust stat if available. If logos are not provided in content, reserve a logo wall component slot with placeholder-safe structure. Keep this section immediately below hero for proof-first scanning.

Do not use grid-inside-grid. Build as two sequential product blocks, each with a strong section headline, descriptive paragraph, and a readable feature card list. For Seedream 4.5, present 5 feature cards in a 2-column list layout within the section. For Seedance 1.5 Pro, present 5 feature cards in a 2-column list layout. Use white cards on a light section background, with concise icon areas even if icons are not provided. Maintain clear separation between the two product blocks with subhead labels.

Add a dedicated video gallery section because the page context explicitly requests it. Use a main preview panel with supporting thumbnail rail or carousel of sample output states. The gallery should be aligned to Seedance 1.5 Pro outcomes and can also include image examples for Seedream if needed. Keep interaction structure Figma-ready with a main visual slot, thumbnail component, and caption area.

Use only the available plan content from the input. Create two pricing cards: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Since prices are empty, build cards with price placeholders, include checklist items from the plan includes, and reserve space for CTA buttons. Keep the card hierarchy consistent with Techjockey pricing patterns, but avoid showing fake pricing values.

Add a fixed-style CTA strip near the end of the page to reinforce conversion. Use a strong accent background, concise benefit line, and primary CTA labeled Generate with AI. Keep this section distinct from hero so the page maintains a conversion anchor without repeating the hero design.
Include standard marketplace footer structure with brand, utility links, and compliance/support items. Keep it compact and consistent with Techjockey site patterns.

figmaExecutionNotes: Use dark hero background with white/light text; avoid a white hero.
Do not add a form because the input does not support one.
Do not add testimonials, news, or why-Techjockey because they are unsupported or explicitly disabled.
Keep trust logos immediately after hero and make them more prominent than badges.
Avoid nested grids inside the features section; use sequential product blocks with readable card lists.
Ensure the full page is represented in the frame, not only the hero.
Maintain mobile parity: stacked hero, single-column feature cards, vertical gallery stacking, and full-width pricing cards.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for premium visual content creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-width dark editorial hero with a layered background mesh and subtle grid lines. Place the copy in a left-weighted glass panel that slightly overlaps the visual stage, while the right side becomes a premium showcase zone with stacked product render cards: one for Seedream outputs and one for Seedance video preview. Make the video element a preview card with a clear play affordance rather than autoplay, so the hero feels controlled and enterprise-ready. Keep the amber brand accent on CTA buttons, chip highlights, and micro-UI strokes. Add a few floating output thumbnails around the main visual to imply multi-output generation without clutter. This layout is intentionally non-standard to avoid the usual split hero pattern while still delivering strong product clarity and trust.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a split hero, then switch to a compact logo trust band, then a visual-first tabs section, then a dark editorial proof/testimonial block, then a product-pricing contrast, then a final conversion strip.
Alternate background tone every section to avoid same-pattern adjacency.
Use one highly visual showcase section for images and a separate media-rich section for video output.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image and Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance's Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore image generation, video generation, proof, pricing, and a direct demo CTA for professional teams.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark editorial canvas with a right-side output stage, subtle glow edges, and a left copy block that feels magazine-like and premium
sections.designNote: Primary goal: instantly explain what this is and who it is for. Narrative mode: premium creative control with enterprise-grade trust. Trust strategy: logos-first, but still keep the hero continuity with the ad message. Visual dominance: balanced, with slightly stronger media emphasis. CTA aggression: strong but not pushy. Recommended hero style: split-left-text-right-image. Keep the headline explicit about AI image and video generation, the subheadline focused on professionals and enterprise teams, and the CTA button label exactly 'Get started' in accent at 100% opacity.

Use 3-6 recognisable enterprise logos if available; if not, replace with a clean metric strip. Since the source data does not provide logos, use a restrained metric/proof strip under a compact trust heading. Keep this section short and highly legible to satisfy warm-traffic proof expectations without interrupting momentum.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: 3 steps from prompt to polished output

sections.designNote: This is the required under-60-seconds explanation, but framed as a concise editorial workflow rather than a generic SaaS process. Use three large steps with one dominant visual preview panel: 1) describe or upload, 2) refine image or video output, 3) export branded visuals. Keep copy short and action-oriented. CTA button text must still be 'Get started'.

Two product blocks must not feel generic or repeated. Lead with Seedream 4.5 as the first product block because it matches the image-generation intent and is the most immediately useful feature set. Use tabs with a preview panel for the 5+ image features: Text–Image Alignment, High-Resolution Output, Typographic Rendering, Multi-Image Composition, and Structural Fidelity. The second product block for Seedance 1.5 Pro should switch to a more cinematic split-panel list or accordion-with-visual treatment to break rhythm, foregrounding video generation, audio-visual sync, lip-sync, camera control, and speed. Keep each block editorial, not grid-heavy.

Use proof here as industry-specific credibility rather than a broad testimonial wall. Since the user requires logos as the main proof type but none are supplied, this section should blend a compact proof line with the strongest quoted validation from creative and marketing roles. Because there are 5 testimonials, use a carousel or spotlight treatment instead of a flat grid. Keep the visual treatment darker and more cinematic than the product section so the page gains contrast.

Do not add a generic all-features dump. Focus on the 1-2 reasons the visitor clicked: professional-grade image generation for ads/posters/branded visuals, and synchronized AI video for branded content and storytelling. Use one large spotlight visual on one side and a compact supporting feature stack on the other. This section should feel more tactile and output-led than the earlier product tabs.

Pricing should stay secondary to capability, but it still needs to feel enterprise-ready. Use two highlighted cards with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro, each with concise inclusions and a clear quote-oriented path. Keep the visual treatment restrained and slightly denser than the preceding feature showcase to signal decision readiness. Button text remains 'Get started' where a button is used.

Final conversion section should be short, confident, and direct. Use a dark floating card with one strong line that reinforces seeing the product in action, not just signing up. This is the endpoint of the warm-traffic sequence, so make it the clearest action zone on the page. The CTA color must be accent at 100% opacity, full-width on mobile, and the label must be exactly 'Get started'.
Keep the footer minimal and informational, with no additional CTA confusion. It should close the page cleanly after the conversion section without visually competing with it.

blueprint.designPersonality: Premium editorial AI studio for enterprises: dark, intelligent, proof-led, and visually refined, with amber accents, strong logo trust signals, and a showcase-first media presentation.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use large polished product render panels, generated image/video thumbnails, and abstract UI shells that resemble a creative studio workspace. Prioritize a dedicated video gallery section with thumbnail cards, duration labels, play controls, and quality badges. Keep trust logos prominent in a horizontal proof strip if available; otherwise, use a clean metric strip.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-screen, full-width top banner with brand/logo placement, large headline, concise supporting copy, and bullet-point value props; hero content is vertically stacked rather than split-media.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Linear landing-page flow: hero/band section first, then conversion form, followed by feature/product sections; content is organized in discrete blocks with clear heading hierarchy and repeated CTA opportunities.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primarily boxed content panels with simple, utilitarian styling; no evidence of glassmorphism or decorative overlays. Cards emphasize structure, borders, and readable spacing over visual effects.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA appears in the hero and repeats within product sections; CTA treatment is direct and conversion-oriented, with minimal secondary CTA presence. Action labels should be short and task-based.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing module pattern in the provided reference HTML. If used, it should remain secondary to lead capture and feature explanation.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not enough HTML provided to infer footer structure; likely a standard informational footer if present elsewhere.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal hero-media treatment in the provided excerpt; the dominant pattern is text-first. Where media exists, it should support claims rather than dominate layout.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature sections use bold section labels, headline, descriptive paragraph, then a list of discrete benefit items. Best extracted pattern: progressive disclosure via stacked feature bullets and repeated CTA per section.
referenceMap.formPattern: Lead-capture form placed immediately after hero as a dedicated conversion block; uses a card container, prominent title, and multiple hidden tracking fields. Keep form visually isolated and easy to scan.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, utility-driven presentation with no clear motion system in the excerpt; if animated elsewhere, it should be subtle and functional rather than decorative.
designNotes: Layout is optimized for conversion and clarity, not visual storytelling.
Use strong hierarchy, compact copy blocks, and straightforward CTA placement.
Maintain consistent container widths and generous vertical spacing between major sections.
Prefer simple icons/checkmarks for benefit lists and avoid heavy illustration dependency.
The page favors an enterprise lead-gen pattern: hero -> form -> feature explanation.

mustHaveMoments: Full-width dark hero with a strong headline, concise subheadline, and short value bullets
Prominent logo trust strip immediately below the hero since logos are the primary trust signal
Primary CTA repeated after each major product section to sustain conversion momentum
Dedicated form section for demo/quote capture, placed before deep feature exploration if possible
Distinct Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro product sections with readable stacked content blocks
Video gallery section showcasing output quality, motion, and audio-visual synchronization
Pricing/quote module kept secondary but visible for enterprise buying evaluation
Testimonial section featuring role-based credibility from creative and marketing professionals
Fixed top strip for persistent navigation and CTA access while scrolling
Footer with standard enterprise contact and policy links
avoidPatterns: Split-screen hero with competing media that weakens the message hierarchy
Glassmorphism, decorative overlays, or visually noisy effects
Grid-inside-grid feature layouts that reduce readability
Additional lead magnet modules that distract from demo booking
Hero content overlapping in a way that harms legibility
Hidden or delayed page loading that prevents immediate scrolling beyond the hero
Form omission when the page goal requires lead capture
Weak or mismatched content hierarchy that blurs the distinction between image and video products
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is a category-style landing page for enterprise buyers evaluating advanced AI image and video generation tools, so the design should optimize for demo booking rather than broad awareness. Since the audience is solution-aware and trusts logos most, the page should lead with a strong product message and immediately reinforce credibility through a logo-first trust strip. The dark theme supports a premium, future-forward positioning and makes visual outputs feel more cinematic. A centered hero is the safest choice because it keeps the headline, supporting copy, and CTAs clear without competing media overload. The structure should stay linear and readable, with stacked feature blocks for Seedream and Seedance rather than complex nested grids. A video gallery is important to demonstrate the product's actual output quality, especially for motion, sync, and branded content use cases. CTAs should repeat naturally across the page, but remain focused on demo/quote actions rather than aggressive purchase language.
